title: You thought your damage disqualified you.
paragraphs:
You thought your damage disqualified you.
But what if your wounds are exactly what God chooses?

The guilt.
The compromise.
The secret habit no one sees.
God still wants to dwell with you.
How can a holy God come near a life that feels… unclean?
How can something sacred be built out of something so flawed?
That’s the question Israel’s wilderness answered.
And it’s the question your soul is still asking.

Tried to clean up.
Tried to pray harder.
Tried to silence the voice that whispers,
“You’re not worthy.”
The Tabernacle—the dwelling place of God—was not built from perfect materials.
It was built from acacia wood.
Wild. Thorny. Scarred by desert heat.

Dry ground.
Relentless sun.
Little nourishment.
You survived things people don’t even know about.
You kept going when your heart was breaking.
You smiled while carrying silent battles.
But here’s the truth you don’t say out loud:
And that’s where shame begins to speak.
“Look at what you still struggle with.”
But God didn’t choose acacia in spite of its environment.
He chose it because of it.

Exodus 25:10–11 (NIV):
“Have them make an ark of acacia wood… Overlay it with pure gold, both inside and out…”
Some scholars interpret the acacia wood as representing humanity—fragile, earthly, imperfect—while the gold represents divine glory, purity, and holiness.
And when the two come together…

John 1:14 (NIV):
“The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory…”

Matthew 27:29 (NIV):
“They twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on his head…”
This is where it breaks you.
Because Jesus didn’t just come near your brokenness—
He took the shame you’ve been hiding.

Not small.
Not excusable.
Not ignorable.

Romans 3:23 (NIV):
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
The part religion often misses, but the Gospel shouts:

Romans 5:8 (NIV):
“But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when you got your act together.
While you were still in it.
And still went to the cross.
Because shame was never meant to be your identity.
God doesn’t build His dwelling with perfect people.
You think your story disqualifies you.
God says it qualifies you for grace.
The acacia wood didn’t become gold.
And you don’t become righteous by effort.

2 Corinthians 5:21 (NIV):
“God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.”

Your sin → His sacrifice
Your shame → His righteousness
Your brokenness → His glory
But here’s the part many avoid:

Acts 3:19 (NIV):
“Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out…”
It’s turning away from the very thing that’s been slowly destroying you.
How long will you keep carrying what Jesus already paid for?
How long will you let shame speak louder than the cross?
You don’t need another self-help strategy.
Because the same God who chose acacia wood—
But only if you let Him cover you.
And receive what you’ve been resisting:
Say it in your own words if you need to.
“Jesus, I’m done hiding. I give You my sin, my shame, my whole life. Cover me. Change me. Be my Savior.”

John 3:16 (NIV):
“For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.”
They need this more than you think.
